title: No Bunkers, No Mercy
theme: Royal Ashdown Forest's hazard-free heathland needs no bunkers to inflict carnage, scattering the field across three separate leaderboards on TEG's first visit to East Sussex.
opening_hook: Royal Ashdown Forest has no bunkers at all, and still found a way to hand out a 12, two separate 9s and a nine-hole, 22-shot collapse before anyone had reached the turn for lunch.

round_story.subject: Jon Baker's net 2 survives a quintuple bogey at the 14th to post the best Trophy score of the day
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the best round of the day by the Trophy's own net-vs-par metric and hands Baker the outright lead after round one, even though his own eight-round TEG history rates it as one of his shakier net-to-par efforts.
round_story.shape: Baker traded the outright net-vs-par lead back and forth all day, drawing level four separate times without ever pulling clear. A quintuple bogey at the par-4 14th then threatened to end the effort altogether. He answered immediately with back-to-back pars at the 15th and 16th, closing with the best net score in the field and sole control of the Trophy - a round that ranks as just his third-worst net-to-par performance in eight TEG rounds to date, whatever the leaderboard now says.
round_story.standfirst: A quintuple bogey threatened to sink him, but a brace of closing pars gave Jon Baker the best net score of the day and sole control of the TEG 4 Trophy.

race_story.subject: A fractured leaderboard after round one: David Mullin claims the Green Jacket lead on twin birdie recoveries while Henry Meller's 12 at the short 11th plants him at the bottom of the Wooden Spoon
race_story.why_it_matters: It establishes the shape of the whole tournament from day one - no single player dominates across all three competitions, and the Spoon already looks close to settled in tone if not in fact.
race_story.shape: The round's carnage scattered players across all three tables. Mullin, having briefly sat at the bottom of the Spoon race himself after a shaky start, answered with birdies at the 10th and 13th to drag himself into the Green Jacket lead on gross. Meanwhile Henry Meller's calamitous 12 at the par-3 11th - a hole-and-a-half worse than anyone else managed all day - left him rooted at the bottom of the Wooden Spoon by four shots, closing a round in which Baker led the Trophy, Mullin led the Jacket, and the course had the last word on everyone.
race_story.standfirst: David Mullin's birdie recoveries hand him the Green Jacket lead even as Henry Meller's 12 at the short 11th buries him at the bottom of the Wooden Spoon.

discovered_storylines.subject: Gregg Williams's day of whiplash: a fleeting outright Trophy lead off a birdie at the 8th collapses into a nine-hole, 22-shot bleed and the worst gross score of the round
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It shows Ashdown's swings within a single round and leaves Williams already off the pace in both major competitions after round one, having anchored the Wooden Spoon race at three separate points along the way.
discovered_storylines.shape: A horror opening - 13 shots dropped across holes 2 to 6, including a quadruple bogey at the 4th - left Williams anchoring the Spoon early. A birdie at the 8th snapped the run and, remarkably, handed him the outright Trophy lead. The reprieve lasted three holes: a 22-shot collapse over the closing nine, including a five-hole stretch without a single net par, dropped him to the day's worst gross score and out of contention in both competitions.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A single birdie briefly put Gregg Williams top of the Trophy table before a 22-shot collapse over the closing nine buried the round for good.

race_state_note: With four rounds still to play and TEG 4 only just under way, none of these gaps - three shots atop the Trophy, three atop the Jacket, four clear at the bottom of the Spoon - amount to more than a first-day skirmish.
